title: Bible facts: weights, measures, money and the calendar
source: Public-domain reference data compiled from standard biblical reference works (Easton's Bible Dictionary, 1897; Smith's Bible Dictionary, 1884; and the International Standard Bible Encyclopedia, 1915). Values are the usual approximations used in study Bibles and are given as ranges where authorities differ. Nothing here is invented: every unit named is attested in Scripture.
license: Public Domain (facts and measurements are not copyrightable; the wording is this project's own)

weights.name: Gerah
weights.note: The smallest unit of weight in the system; a bean.

weights.name: Beka
weights.note: The weight of the ring Rebekah received.

weights.name: Shekel
weights.note: The basic unit of weight and of money. The 'shekel of the sanctuary' was the standard.

weights.name: Mina (maneh)
weights.note: Also a unit of money (50 shekels of silver).

weights.name: Talent
weights.note: The largest unit. A talent of gold was roughly a year's wages for a labourer multiplied many times over.

measures_dry.name: Seah (satton)
measures_dry.note: The measure Sarah used for the flour.

measures_dry.name: Ephah
measures_dry.note: The standard dry measure; a person's daily bread ration was about an omer.

measures_dry.name: Homer (cor)
measures_dry.note: A donkey-load; the largest dry measure.

measures_liquid.name: Log
measures_liquid.note: The smallest liquid measure; the leper's offering.

measures_liquid.name: Hin
measures_liquid.note: A standard liquid measure; the drink offering.

measures_liquid.name: Bath
measures_liquid.note: The largest liquid measure; about the same as an ephah of dry measure.

money.name: Lepton (mite)
money.note: The widow's mite; the smallest coin.

money.name: Assarion
money.note: Two sparrows sold for an assarion.

money.name: Denarius (penny)
money.value: a day's wage for a labourer
money.scripture: Matt 18:28; Matt 20:2; Matt 20:9; Matt 20:10; Matt 20:13; Mark 6:37; Luke 7:41; Luke 10:35; John 6:7; Rev 6:6
money.note: The standard silver coin of the Roman period; a day's pay.

money.name: Drachma
money.note: Greek silver coin; the lost coin.

money.name: Stater (shekel)
money.note: The coin found in the fish's mouth; temple tax for two.

money.name: Mina
money.scripture: Luke 19:13; Luke 19:16; Luke 19:18; Luke 19:20; Luke 19:24; Luke 19:25
money.note: A unit of money in the parable of the pounds.

money.name: Talent (of silver)
money.scripture: Matt 18:24; Matt 25:15; Matt 25:20; Matt 25:22; Matt 25:24; Matt 25:25; Matt 25:28
money.note: The enormous debt in the parable of the unforgiving servant.

calendar_months.name: Tishri (Ethanim)
calendar_months.note: Seventh month; Rosh Hashanah, Yom Kippur, Sukkot.

calendar_months.name: Adar
calendar_months.note: Twelfth month; Purim. A leap month (Adar II) is added in leap years.

festivals.name: Pentecost (Shavuot)
festivals.note: Feast of Weeks; the giving of the Law / the Spirit.

festivals.name: Day of Atonement (Yom Kippur)
festivals.note: The high priest enters the Most Holy Place.

festivals.name: Tabernacles (Sukkot)
festivals.note: Feast of Booths; dwelling in tents.
